title: prefill/ decode pipeline: speculative chunking and stage-overlap optimizations
author: Asha Patel
description: This PR introduces a set of coordinated prefill->decode pipeline optimizations: 1) chunked prefill (split long prefill sequences into smaller chunks that can be scheduled and executed earlier so downstream decode can begin sooner), 2) speculative prefill (start prefill work for likely next-token KV blocks in parallel with latency-sensitive decode work when GPU occupancy allows), and 3) stage overlap scheduling (overlap prefill/kv/compile tasks with decode kernel launches to reduce idle GPU time). The goal is to reduce end-to-end tail latency for typical interactive workloads and improve throughput for mixed prefill+decode traffic. The changes touch the scheduler, KV cache prefetching, kernel launch ordering, and the continuous batching heuristics. Benchmarks show median latency improvements of ~8-12% on web-chat workloads and up to 20% throughput increase for mixed short-prefill workloads in our perf-canary setup. The description below summarizes motivation, design, implementation notes, test coverage, and rollout plan.

diff_snippets: serving/runtime/prefill_chunker.cc: added chunk loop and boundary checks: for (size_t offset=0; offset < seq_len; offset += chunk_size) { prep_chunk(offset, min(chunk_size, seq_len-offset)); schedule_prefill(chunk); }
serving/runtime/speculative_prefill.cc: occupancy check to avoid contention: if (gpu_occupancy > 0.6 && !decode_critical_path()) start_speculative_prefill();
serving/runtime/scheduler.cc: updated schedule order: prefer overlapping prefill tasks with decode kernels using timed-futures and stream assignment
review_comments: Diego: Nice work on the chunker. Please add a few more unit tests around chunk_size==1 and chunk_size==seq_len edge cases. Also verify metrics emitted when speculative prefill is skipped.
Asha: Added unit tests for edge cases and metrics emission; pushed commit e4b1c9d that includes additional tests and telemetry emitters.
Liam: Scheduler changes look good but please ensure no regression on very large sequence lengths (>= 64k). Can we add a perf-canary run for a 64k seq scenario?

Maya: KV prefetch integration is clean. One nit: kv_cache_manager::prefetch now returns a future; please document lifetime semantics for callers. Also request to add a debug metric for prefetch hit/miss post-deploy.
perf_summary: Perf-canary results (NVIDIA A100, mixed chat workload): median total latency reduced by 10.7% across trials; p95 improved by 6-9% depending on model; throughput for mixed short-prefill jobs improved up to 20% under continuous-batcher enabled. Memory overhead for speculative prefill measured at ~3% additional KV allocation in worst-case; speculative work is gated by occupancy heuristics to avoid OOM.
test_plan: Unit tests added for prefill_chunker and speculative_prefill; integration test added to perf-canary config; e2e staging run exercising long-sequence and short-sequence mixed workload; manual verification on dedicated nodes with real customer traces. CI runs full test matrix before merge.
rollback_plan: Feature gated via runtime flags (feature.flags.prefill_chunking, ++speculative_prefill, ++stage_overlap). Default rollout is conservative (disabled for dedicated customers by default). Rollback: flip flags to restore previous scheduler behavior and redeploy; metrics/alerts added to detect regressions in latency or OOM.
migration_notes: No schema changes. KV cache prefetch introduces optional future-returning APIs but provides backward-compatible overloads. Operators can tune chunk_size and occupancy thresholds via runtime config.
docs_added: docs/ops/prefill_decode_optimizations.md contains rationale, configs, rollout guidance, and observed perf numbers. Short changelog paragraph added to release notes.
release_notes: Runtime: Prefill/decode pipeline optimizations (chunked prefill, speculative prefill, stage overlap) to reduce interactive latency and improve throughput. Controlled rollout via runtime feature flags. No breaking changes.
post_merge_actions: Enable feature flag for internal perf cohort on 2026-03-01; monitor perf-canary dashboards and kv cache metrics; follow-up PR will expose fine-grained config via Console.
notes: We ran a small canary across 5 dedicated nodes with production traffic and observed no functional regressions. A follow-up PR will add adaptive chunk sizing based on historical prefix length distributions.
